title: State excise policy litigation - why High Courts get involved often
p1: Why do state excise policies so often end up in High Courts? The surprising part is that many disputes are not just about alcohol rules — they are about how government power is used.
p2: A common misconception is that excise policy decisions are completely beyond challenge. In reality, courts usually do not replace the government’s decision with their own. They examine whether the policy follows the law, treats people fairly, and respects constitutional limits.
p3: State excise policies affect businesses, consumers, and government revenue, so even small changes can create major consequences. A licensing rule, tax change, or restriction may be challenged if affected parties believe the process was unfair or the authority exceeded its powers. The key takeaway: High Courts often step in not to run excise departments, but to ensure that public power is exercised legally and fairly.
conclusion: Do you think courts should have a bigger role in reviewing state excise policies, or should governments have wider freedom to make such decisions?
